subject: science
intro: Hi, I'm Ms. Johnson, 7th grade science. Let's plan a lesson on food webs and how energy moves through an ecosystem.

beats.narration: The title tells students what to track: the energy.
This standard is about modeling how matter cycles and energy flows among living and non-living parts of an ecosystem.
"Trace" means they have to follow the arrows, not just draw them.
beats.text: Students will be able to build a food web model and trace how energy flows from producers to consumers and decomposers.

beats.narration: Almost every chain leads back to the sun, which is a powerful realization.
beats.text: "You ate lunch today. Where did that energy originally come from?" Students trace it back as far as they can.

beats.narration: Arrow direction is the most common error, so I emphasize it heavily.
beats.text: Model a simple food chain, then connect it into a web. Emphasize that arrows point in the direction energy flows, from the eaten to the eater. Introduce the 10% rule with a pyramid.

beats.narration: The yarn web shows interconnection in a way a drawing can't.
beats.text: Yarn web: each student is an organism card. Pass yarn to connect who eats whom. Then "remove" one organism and see who is affected.

beats.narration: The "what if" question checks understanding of producers as the energy base.
beats.text: Draw a food web with at least 5 organisms. What would happen to the web if the producers disappeared?

outro: Personal hook, model, physical web, prediction. Your turn.
